questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get far away from Denmark, get acquainted with a different legal system than the Danish one, wanted to go somewhere warm, wanted to go somewhere with many Danes and wanted to live in a big city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to find the information I needed - both the information I needed from KU and the information I needed from my host university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance, but I had received regular emails from my host university with information on how and when to register for courses, what events were organised on campus for exchange students, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found an apartment with three other exchange students from Denmark. It was relatively easy as there are many Australian accommodation websites. My advice would be to go to Australia and book a hotel/hostel for the first few weeks and only find accommodation when you arrive. Many places require you to turn up for viewings in order to get the property.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I thought it was nice to live off-campus. There was the possibility to live in a bigger apartment, the price was the same as if you lived on campus and I had the opportunity to live with some Danes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to write a lot of information for them, upload many documents etc., but the process was relatively easy as I was guided through everything and they clearly and easily stated what information they needed from me.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: During the process, I got help from both UCPH and UNSW. I received help via email, where both parties were quick to respond to my questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had to wish for about ten courses for the host university. Unfortunately, I couldn't rank which ones I wanted the most. I didn't get the ones I wanted most - but I did get the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Set aside a lot of time for it and familiarise yourself with the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a good experience.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was appropriate and comparable to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Attendance at classes was compulsory, there were regular mandatory assignments, mandatory presentations and more focus on student involvement.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Worlds Religion 
Conflict of Laws 
Criminal Law 
Criminology: An Introduction

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend them all. All the courses had exams at home, which I thought was nice as several UNSW courses have physical exams that have to be written by hand. Worlds Religion, Criminal Law and Criminology: An Introduction were all easy courses at a relatively manageable academic level. The reading load was not very high and the courses were all introductory courses. Conflict of Laws was really exciting (the most exciting course of them all), but also really difficult. There was an insane amount of syllabus and you had to know a lot of rules, including a lot of common law concepts, which can be difficult when you are not used to the legal system from home.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think there were any unexpected expenses.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices were much the same as in Denmark. However, it was cheaper to go out to eat and buy a cup of coffee, while it was a bit more expensive to buy groceries.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many activities and societies.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UNSW is a really big university, so all the societies, clubs, activities etc. that you can imagine were possible. There were all kinds of sports clubs and there were film clubs, creative clubs, party clubs, religious clubs, loneliness clubs, exchange student clubs etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I wasn't a member of any clubs, as I met a lot of other people through my courses, knew people from home in Denmark etc., so I didn't need it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to a surf camp, travelling around a lot of Australian cities, experiencing nature, going to the Blue Mountains, going to Slip'n (a bar where all Danes in Sydney meet on the first Thursday of the month), experiencing all of Sydney's many tourist attractions, going for a run and enjoying the beaches.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the culture is similar to Denmark in many ways. However, Australians are much more welcoming than Danes, so that's just positive.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to other students when you have classes, join associations and attend events at university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find any challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That the locals were so nice, helpful and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy it - time goes by quickly
2. Don't spend too much time studying for the courses - have fun.
3. Be approachable, talk to people at university, come to classes and be social

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, there isn't.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Get to know a different school system, be challenged personally and academically, develop my professional English, meet a lot of people, get the opportunity to get to know another culture, be on my own (away from busy Denmark) and get the opportunity to live in another country for free (I applied for and received a lot of grants that could pay for all my expenses while I was away).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from friends and family. Even though there is FaceTime and you can easily text with them, it can be a challenge to find time to do so due to the time difference.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
